findings.issue_text: `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30-59`

*Why it matters:* this is a privilege escalation across every app routed through this helper — Hubspot, Salesforce, Stripe, Tandem, Webex, MS Teams. A `MEMBER`-role user can attach credentials to the team. For `stripepayment/api/callback.ts:44` that means a non-admin member can bind their own Stripe account to the team's payment configuration. The `state` param carrying `teamId` is an unsigned, attacker-shapeable query string, so an install link can be crafted to target any team the victim belongs to.

*Why it matters:* two consequences. (a) The stated contract "assume any property with a number is the expiry" is not implemented — there is no expiry validation at all. (b) `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, so in sync mode the parse output is `{ access_token }` *only* — `expiry_date`/`expires_in` are dropped. Downstream, `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264` spreads that over the existing credentials, leaving the stale (already-expired) `expires_in` in place, which means a token refresh round-trip on literally every calendar call.

A `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` is `undefined` and `token.access_token` throws `TypeError`. Caught at line 103; message isn't `"invalid_grant"`, so it returns stale credentials silently. Sync never works for Google Calendar and fails invisibly.

This moves *away* from DRY and creates a silent mismatch if the config slug ever changes. Revert to `appConfig.slug`. Line 62's `findFirst` on `(userId, appId)` silently picks one row if duplicates exist.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101`

adjudication.rationale:
Yes, there is a concrete bug introduced in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` around the updated refresh flow. The code now does:

```ts
const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);
await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } });
```

But `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` (added in this diff) returns the *Zod safeParse result object* (i.e., `{ success: boolean, data?: ... }`), not the parsed credential payload itself. Previously the code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returns the actual credential object.

As written, this will persist the safeParse wrapper object into `credential.key`, breaking expected shape for later reads/uses of the credential (it will contain `success`/`data` instead of the token fields). A reasonable fix would be to store `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` (or change `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to return `.data`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11`

adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. `z.string().toString()` produces the literal string "[object Object]", so these are not dynamic/index signatures; they become a single fixed property key and the second entry overwrites the first due to duplicate key names. As a result, the schema does not actually validate “any numeric property is the expiry” and is effectively just `{ access_token: string }` with one optional junk key, which is a real correctness bug in the diff.

Downstream, `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264` spreads that over the existing credentials, leaving the stale (already-expired) `expires_in` in place, which means a token refresh round-trip on literally every calendar call.

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29`

adjudication.rationale:
In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` the webhook “auth” check compares the incoming header value to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is not set (i.e., `undefined` at runtime), and the request also omits the header (so `req.headers[...]` is `undefined`), the comparison becomes `undefined !== undefined`, which is false, meaning the request is accepted and the endpoint is effectively unauthenticated (bypass).

This is a real security/correctness issue introduced by the diff because the code does not enforce that `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (and header name) are configured before allowing requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:84-95` — overwrites `credential.key` wholesale with the response body, which under sync drops `refresh_token` permanently.
`larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84` — `handleLarkError` expects Lark's `{code, data:{...}}` envelope, which a generic sync endpoint won't produce.

adjudication.rationale: In `larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh call was changed to use `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. That helper will, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set and `credential.userId` is truthy, return the `fetch()` Response from the *generic* sync endpoint instead of Lark’s `/authen/v1/refresh_access_token` Response. Immediately after, the code still does `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)`, which (by usage/name) is a Lark-specific response/error parser intended for Lark’s response shape. A generic sync endpoint is not expected to return Lark’s `{ code, data: ... }` envelope, so this is a concrete compatibility/correctness bug introduced by the diff when credential sync is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **19. Webhook cleanups.** `app-credential.ts:16` has a stray empty `/** */` JSDoc. Line 34 fetches the entire user row for an existence check — add `select: { id: true }`. Lines 40-50 query `prisma.app` and then re-look-up `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]`; the DB round-trip adds nothing the metadata lookup doesn't already provide. adjudication.rationale: All points cited are either style/performance suggestions or speculative data-integrity concerns, not clear defects verifiable from the diff. The `/** */` is a harmless stray comment. Fetching the full user row instead of `select: {id:true}` is a minor optimization, not a bug. The `prisma.app` lookup before using `appStoreMetadata[slug]` may be intentional to ensure the app exists in the DB (e.g., enabled/installed) and isn’t provably redundant from the diff. The concern about `findFirst` “silently picking one row if duplicates exist” depends on schema/constraints not shown here, so it’s not a verifiable problem in this diff.
